note: Seed set curated from web research (Jul 2026). Auto-refreshed by scripts/update-tracking.mjs via the Anthropic API + web search; new items are merged and de-duplicated by URL.

items.title: New documents detail nine-figure, Silicon Valley-funded abundance movement
items.summary: The American Prospect reports on internal 'Abundance Capital Stack' documents pledging up to $260M/year from John Arnold, Dustin Moskovitz and Steve Ballmer, though organizers say actual grants are closer to $40M. It ties the money to tech founders including Stripe's Patrick Collison, the same figures bankrolling YIMBY/progress efforts now crossing into UK and European planning debates.

items.title: The monthly meet-up dedicated to fixing Ireland's infrastructure crisis
items.summary: TheJournal.ie profiles Progress Ireland, a five-person YIMBY-inspired think tank led by Sean Keyes and backed by Stripe billionaire John Collison. Its 'garden homes' proposal was adopted by the Irish government; critics such as People Before Profit's Paul Murphy frame it as corporate influence on Irish housing policy.

items.title: Pour Demain and SaferAI host AI-safety roundtable at European Parliament
items.summary: Swiss policy think tank Pour Demain and France's SaferAI co-hosted a European Parliament roundtable, 'Moonshots in Reliable, Safe & Secure AI,' with MEPs Michael McNamara and Sergey Lagodinsky. Around 40 participants discussed AI safety audits and European strategic adoption, showing the EA/Open Phil-linked safety network working directly inside EU institutions.

items.title: 2025 CEO letter: Coefficient Giving directed over $1 billion
items.summary: Alexander Berger's 2025 CEO letter confirms Coefficient Giving (formerly Open Philanthropy) directed over $1 billion in 2025, the most in its history, raising total giving more than 50% and more than doubling non-Good Ventures funding to over $200M. It cites two new funds, a nearly all-new leadership team, and the rebrand as milestones of its multi-donor transition.

items.title: Coefficient's Global Growth Fund and European effective-giving grantees
items.summary: The 2025 CEO letter notes a mid-2025 Global Growth Fund for low- and middle-income economies and highlights European effective-giving grantees: Dutch platform Doneer Effectief (over $9M raised in 2025, up from ~€6.3M in 2024) and Germany's Effektiv Spenden. These flow from Coefficient's effective-giving RFP, marking direct money into European EA infrastructure.

items.title: Court of Justice of EU hears how Commission failed citizens on cage ban
items.summary: The CJEU heard a landmark case by Compassion in World Farming, Eurogroup for Animals, Animal Equality and LAV over the Commission's failure to deliver its 2021 'End the Cage Age' pledge. Judges pressed the Commission on refusing a legislative timeline, in the first case holding it accountable for a European Citizens' Initiative affecting nearly 300 million caged EU farm animals.

items.title: Albert Schweitzer Foundation's German Broiler Initiative hits 2025 milestone
items.summary: The Albert Schweitzer Foundation reported that its Broiler Initiative secured an animal-welfare commitment from retailer Edeka, bringing over 110 German companies on board including Aldi, Kaufland, Lidl and Rewe. Aldi and Tegut completed full own-brand conversions, while McDonald's and Burger King remained the most prominent holdouts.

items.title: European Commission adopts proposal for the EU Biotech Act
items.summary: The Commission published its Biotech Act proposal, including biosecurity provisions: a list of 'biotechnology products of concern' restricted to legitimate uses, and a mandate that benchtop nucleic-acid synthesis devices sold in the EU carry built-in screening for 'sequences of concern.' It marks the EU's first move toward mandatory DNA-synthesis screening, a long-standing EA/biosecurity policy ask.

items.title: EU backslides on AI rules — what does it mean for Switzerland?
items.summary: Swissinfo reports the Commission's 'Digital Omnibus' plan to delay parts of the AI Act, giving large tech firms more time to comply, attributed partly to US pressure during tariff talks. AI-safety NGOs treated the rollback as a setback for the Code of Practice framework they had helped shape, and it may influence Switzerland's own AI legislation.

items.title: L214 files complaint against Breton pig farms and Carrefour
items.summary: French animal-welfare group L214 filed a legal complaint against two Brittany pig farms linked to Cooperl and retailer Carrefour, alleging mistreatment and deceptive commercial practices including routine tail docking and tooth grinding. Carrefour called the practices 'absolutely unacceptable' and suspended supplies from one farm pending an external audit.

items.title: Open Philanthropy becomes Coefficient Giving, expanding work with multiple donors
items.summary: Open Philanthropy rebranded as Coefficient Giving on Nov 18, 2025, shifting from serving one anchor donor (Good Ventures) to running multi-donor pooled funds any philanthropist can join. CEO Alexander Berger framed the name around amplifying cost-effective, globally-focused impact, including its expanding European grantmaking.

items.title: Billionaires are jumping into Coefficient Giving's pooled philanthropy
items.summary: Forbes reported that funders beyond Dustin Moskovitz and Cari Tuna — including Stripe's Patrick Collison, Lucy Southworth and Bill Gates — are backing Coefficient Giving's themed funds, which drew over $200M in outside commitments in 2025 (up from ~$100M the prior year). Flagship vehicles include the Abundance & Growth Fund and the Lead Exposure Action Fund.

items.title: John Collison: Ireland is going backwards. Here's how to get it moving
items.summary: Stripe co-founder John Collison published an Irish Times essay arguing Ireland has failed to build housing and infrastructure due to over-delegation to unelected agencies and counterproductive environmental mandates. He endorsed Progress Ireland's blueprint of 25 ideas to deliver 300,000 homes, importing US-style abundance framing into Irish politics.

items.title: Why Open Philanthropy is doubling down on abundance
items.summary: Inside Philanthropy profiled the $120M-over-three-years Abundance & Growth Fund, seeded with $60M from Good Ventures plus an undisclosed sum from Stripe's Patrick Collison and other donors, led by program officer Matt Clancy. Focus spans housing/YIMBY, energy, innovation and clinical-trial reform; reporting emphasized US policy, with international expansion flagged as a future possibility.

items.title: Abundance for the 99 Percent
items.summary: Jacobin published a socialist defense of Klein and Thompson's 'Abundance' by Matt Huber, Leigh Phillips and Fred Stafford, arguing the book targets bottlenecks constraining state capacity rather than merely repackaging neoliberalism. The piece captures the left's contested reception of the abundance agenda now crossing into UK and European planning debates.

items.title: The Future Society's response to the EU's GPAI Code of Practice
items.summary: The Future Society, an Open Phil-linked AI-governance nonprofit active in Brussels, criticized the final EU Code of Practice for General-Purpose AI, arguing US tech firms won weakening changes in a fourth drafting round. It flagged post-deployment-only reporting, eliminated whistleblower protections, no emergency-preparedness requirements, and excessive provider discretion over risk assessment.

items.title: Priorities to uphold European biosecurity in 2025
items.summary: The Centre for Future Generations, with Pandemic Action Network, RAND Europe, IBBIS and Pour Demain, issued a briefing urging the EU to regulate DNA-synthesis screening, create a permanent Commission expert group on biosecurity threats, and tie pathogen-research funding to biosecurity standards. The longtermism-linked CFG's agenda foreshadowed the Biotech Act's screening provisions.

items.title: EU's AI rules set to be handed on a silver plate to corporate lobbyists
items.summary: Corporate Europe Observatory reported that Big Tech firms secured privileged access to workshops and Commission meetings while the EU AI Act's GPAI Code of Practice was drafted, with civil society sidelined. The critique warns of a 'Delay, Pause, Deregulate' strategy and flags conflicts of interest among consulting firms hired to help draft the rules.

items.title: SaferAI receives €170,227 for AI risk-management work feeding EU AI Act
items.summary: In H1 2025, French AI-safety org SaferAI received €170,227 via German-Swiss platform Effektiv Spenden (from its 'Ensuring Safe AI' and 'Safeguarding the Future' funds). SaferAI, which builds frameworks to rate AI companies' risk management, contributed to formulating the EU AI Act's Code of Practice, illustrating EA-aligned money routed into EU policy work.

items.title: UK's ARIA announces £45m for 21 'climate cooling' research projects
items.summary: The UK's Advanced Research + Invention Agency (ARIA) committed £45M to 21 solar-geoengineering projects, including five small-scale outdoor experiments, making the UK the world's largest single funder of solar-geoengineering research. The programme spans Arctic sea-ice thickening, cloud brightening, and governance/ethics, exemplifying the UK's ARPA-style progress agenda.
